subject: DPA follow-up: residency & retention clarifications for pilot
messages:
From: Katie Jordan <katie@olive-sys.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-25T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions: DPA retention & residency for pilot

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. Procurement here at Olive asked me to follow up with a couple of concrete items we need captured in the DPA for the EU pilot:

- Residency: Can Redwood guarantee processing and primary storage (including logs) will remain in the EU for the pilot data set? If not, what are the fallback geographies and triggers?
- Retention by data class: We need default retention buckets and the ability to set shorter TTLs per dataset. Suggested: PII (30 days), session telemetry (90 days), model usage telemetry (180 days). Can you confirm what you support today?
- Backups & snapshots: How long are weekly backups retained? Are backups ever stored outside the EU? What is the erase process for snapshots and how quickly can you produce proof of deletion if requested?
- Evidence: We will require operational evidence of erasure (delete manifest or signed attestation) within a customer SLA window. What SLA can you commit for producing that evidence?

I attached our vendor questionnaire (procurement section) — answered fields would be ideal. If helpful we can do a short 20–30 min call this week to align.

Thanks,

Katie Jordan
Head of Procurement, Olive Systems
procurement@olive-sys.com
Attachment: olive-vendor-questionnaire-20260924.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Jordan <katie@olive-sys.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-25T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: DPA retention & residency for pilot

Hi Katie —

Really helpful list, thanks. Quick summary up front: we can operate the pilot with EU-only primary processing and storage, and we have config knobs for retention by data class. Backups are kept per-region but there are operational nuances (see below).

I attached a short explainer that maps our current defaults and the redline language we'd propose for the DPA section on retention & residency. High-level points:

- Residency: Primary storage and active processing for pilot workloads can be limited to the EU region (no outbound replication) if Olive requires it. We would need to lock the model variant and region in the deployment config for the duration of the pilot. Fallback routing to non-EU regions is available only under capacity emergency with prior notice and a documented escalation path.
- Retention by class: Our configurable defaults today are: PII-like transcripts (30 days), session-level telemetry (90 days), product usage telemetry (180 days). These are adjustable pre-deployment and via a tenant-level policy.
- Backups & snapshots: Weekly backups (snapshots) are created by default and retained 90 days in EU regions. Snapshots are held for operational restore and disaster recovery; they are only replicated outside the EU in the event of region-wide disaster recovery, and only with contractually-bound subprocessors.
- Proof of deletion: We can produce an erase manifest (list of object IDs, timestamps, and the operator run id) within 10 business days as a standard SLA. Expedited attestation (3 business days) is available for an additional fee/enterprise add-on.

I'll loop in Karthik, Marcus and Laura to confirm the technical/ops/legal wording and to surface any limits we should call out in the DPA redline.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-retention-explainer.pdf

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-25T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Questions: DPA retention & residency for pilot

Team — forwarding Olive's procurement questions and my initial draft answers. Core asks we need to confirm: snapshot retention policy, scope of cross-border backup replication, and acceptable SLA for erase manifests.

Proposed redline (suggestion for DPA section 4.2 — Retention & Deletion):
"Supplier shall retain Customer Data only for the period necessary to provide Services, with the following default retention periods by data class unless Customer specifies otherwise prior to deployment: (a) Personal identifiers & transcripts — 30 days; (b) session telemetry — 90 days; (c) product usage telemetry — 180 days. Backups/snapshots shall be retained no longer than 90 days unless required for legal hold; snapshots may be replicated outside the EU only for region-failover scenarios with prior notice to the Customer. Upon Customer request to delete Customer Data, Supplier will execute deletion from active storage within X days and will provide an erase manifest within 10 business days; deletion from backups/snapshots will follow the snapshot retention cycle unless a proactive purge is requested and mutually agreed."

Questions for you:
- Karthik: Can we commit to the 10 business day erase-manifest SLA? Can snapshots be proactively purged earlier than the configured retention, and how long does a purge job take end-to-end?
- Marcus: What operational evidence can we generate for a purge (log entries, job ids, signed attestation)?
- Laura: Any legal concerns about the current wording ("shall" vs "reasonable efforts"; onshore replication carveouts) or procurement asking for a 30-day limit for all classes?

Attachments: proposed-redline-retention.txt

Thanks — Vanessa
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-25T11:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions: DPA retention & residency for pilot

Vanessa — quick technical confirmation and recommended tweaks below. Happy to jump on a call if you want to walk the flow.

- Erase-manifest SLA: We can produce object-level erase manifests within 10 business days for active storage deletions; for snapshot purges it depends on retention tier and index rebuild windows. For EU weekly snapshots retained 90d our purge pipeline can target a snapshot and trigger logical deletion within 48 hours, but final low-level block reclamation can take up to 14 days depending on underlying storage compaction. The manifest will reflect the logical deletion timestamp and the operator job id.
- Proactive snapshot purge: Yes, we can schedule a proactive purge of selected snapshots; in our experience planning and validation mean a 3–7 day operational window to ensure no service impact.
- Cross-border backup replication: We do not replicate backups outside the EU unless the customer opts into global DR. In that case, replication is only to vendor-approved DR zones and only under explicit contractual authorization.
- Evidence types: We can provide a signed operational attestation (pdf), erase manifest (.csv with object ids + timestamps), and traceable job ids with operator audit logs.

Suggested redline tweaks: change "shall provide" to "will provide an erase manifest and attestation within the SLA window, subject to the technical constraints of snapshot compaction and storage reclamation." That preserves a firm SLA for active data while accounting for backups.

Attachment: backup-retention-matrix.csv

Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

Vanessa / team —

Appreciate the detailed responses and the draft language. Olive can accept a split model: 30 days for transcripts/PII in primary storage, 90 days for backups/snapshots, with the erase manifest for active deletions provided within 10 business days. For snapshot purges we understand there may be a compaction window — please add explicit language in the DPA that final block-level reclamation may take up to 14 days and that the erase manifest will show logical deletion dates and operator job ids.

Can we set up a 30-minute call tomorrow to confirm the final redline and procurement signoff? Prefer 09:00–11:00 CET. Also please attach the attestation template you mentioned and the short explainer PDF for our legal team.

Thanks,

Katie Jordan
